questions.question: Explain Darwin's theory of natural selection with an example.
questions.solution:
**Darwin's theory (1859):** Organisms produce more offspring than can survive. Individuals with favorable variations survive and reproduce (natural selection). Over generations, favorable traits become common.

**Postulates:**
1. Overproduction — more offspring produced
2. Variation — individuals differ
3. Struggle for existence — limited resources
4. Survival of the fittest — better adapted survive
5. Heredity — favorable traits passed on

**Example:** Industrial melanism in moths — dark moths survived better in soot-covered trees during Industrial Revolution.
questions.knowledgeNote: Darwin called it 'descent with modification.' Modern synthesis combines Darwin with genetics.
questions.answer: **Darwin's theory of natural selection (1859, On the Origin of Species):** **(1) Overproduction:** every species produces far more offspring than can survive (Darwin: 'more are born than can possibly survive'). **(2) Struggle for existence:** because food, space and mates are limited, offspring compete — with each other, with other species and with the environment. **(3) Variation:** individuals within a species differ in inherited traits (size, speed, colour, resistance). **(4) Survival of the fittest (natural selection):** individuals with variations best suited to the environment survive and reproduce more successfully ('differential survival and reproduction'); the less-fit are eliminated. **(5) Origin of new species:** favourable variations accumulate over generations; populations diverge until new species arise. **Example — industrial melanism in the peppered moth (*Biston betularia*):** before industrialisation, pale (typica) moths camouflaged on lichen-covered tree trunks and birds ate the rare dark mutants. In soot-blackened English industrial cities the trunks darkened and lichens died — now the **dark (carbonaria) moths were camouflaged and the pale ones were eaten**; within decades the dark form rose from <1% to ~95% of city populations. Pollution control reversed the trend — the environment, not the moth's will, selected the form. **Deep point:** selection acts on *existing* variation, it does not create it — the dark mutants existed before the smoke; the environment merely decided which mutation would matter.
